Finally, we construct an exact growth-diagram sampler for finite reflected truncations and prove that their laws converge in total variation to the full Gibbs measure on every fixed rail-yard graph with finitely many columns as the truncation level tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyang Li

item.title: A Non-Markovian Approach to a Stochastic Rumor Dynamics with Cognitive Deliberation
item.description: arXiv:2407.07170v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a non-Markovian rumor model on a complete graph of $n$ vertices, integrating the classical interactional framework of Daley and Kendall (1964) with modern cognitive insights into misinformation. Unlike traditional Markovian models, our approach incorporates a deliberation delay -- a decision-making window where individuals evaluate information before committing to dissemination or refutation. We establish a Functional Law of Large Numbers (FLLN) and a Functional Central Limit Theorem (FCLT) to characterize the asymptotic behavior and diffusion-scaled fluctuations of the process.
item.dc:creator: Cristian F. Coletti, Denis A. Luiz

item.title: A phase transition for the cokernels of random band matrices over the p-adic integers
item.description: arXiv:2408.13037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbf{B}_n$ be an $n\times n$ Haar-uniform band matrix over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with band width $w_n$. We prove that $\text{cok}(\mathbf{B}_n)$ has Cohen-Lenstra limiting distribution if and only if \[\lim_{n\to\infty} \left(w_n-\log_p(n)\right)=+\infty.\]
item.dc:creator: Andr\'as M\'esz\'aros

item.title: Smallest gaps of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas
item.description: arXiv:2507.23502v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas with a general potential at the determinantal temperature, or equivalently, the eigenvalues of random normal matrices. We prove that the smallest gaps between particles are typically of order $n^{-3/4}$, and that the associated joint point process of gap locations and gap sizes, after rescaling the gaps by $n^{3/4}$, converges to a Poisson point process. As a consequence, we show that the $k$-th smallest rescaled gap has a limiting density proportional to $x^{4k-1}e^{-\frac{\mathcal{J}}{4}x^{4}}$, where $\mathcal{J}=\pi^{2}\int \rho(z)^{3}d^{2}z$ and $\rho$ is the density of the equilibrium measure. This generalizes a result of Shi and Jiang beyond the quadratic potential.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Charlier

item.title: Density estimation for exponential functionals of subordinators
item.description: arXiv:2509.17199v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Exponential functionals of subordinators play a key role in probability theory and arise in numerous applications, yet explicit density formulas have until now been available only in a limited number of special settings. This paper provides a general remedy. First, we obtain a closed-form representation of the density for the entire class of integer-valued subordinators (compound Poisson processes with positive integer jump sizes) in the form of a rapidly converging series whose coefficients obey a simple recurrence; we further extend the construction to include drift by means of an explicit iterative scheme. Second, we propose a general approximation method for arbitrary driftless subordinators, including cases where the L\'{e}vy measure has continuous support. By discretizing the L\'{e}vy measure, we generate a sequence of explicit, computable densities that is proved to converge to the true density. Together, these results greatly broaden the theory of exponential functionals, transforming a problem previously tractable only in rare instances into one that is either explicitly solvable or can be systematically approximated for the full class of subordinators. The resulting formulas enable fast and accurate computations for financial modelling, insurance risk assessment, and stochastic simulation, while the approximation procedure provides a robust and stable alternative to existing numerical methods. The unified framework --- linking pantograph equations, $q$-calculus, and Poisson approximation --- also opens avenues for analyzing more general decreasing functionals and drifted subordinators with general L\'{e}vy measures.
item.dc:creator: Dongdong Hu, Hasanjan Sayit, Weixuan Xia

item.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
item.description: arXiv:2510.09206v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-R\'enyi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Fu, Jiange Li

item.title: Sub-Diffusive Black--Scholes Model and Structure-Preserving Girsanov Transform
item.description: arXiv:2511.10371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a sub-diffusive Black--Scholes model in which stock prices are governed by stochastic differential equations driven by sub-diffusions. The model captures the periods of low trading activity observed in bear markets, and it contains the classical Black--Scholes model as a special case. The sub-diffusive spot market is arbitrage-free but, in general, incomplete. We study the pricing of European contingent claims in this model. To this end, we establish a structure-preserving Girsanov transform for sub-diffusions. We use it to identify the minimal martingale measure of the model. This measure is the unique equivalent martingale measure under which the discounted stock prices are martingales driven by sub-diffusions with the same law as the original ones. Using this measure, we price every contingent claim in $L^p$ with $p>2$. For each such claim, we construct a replicating strategy that is mean self-financing and minimizes the local risk, and whose value process gives the price process of the claim. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the price of a European call option. We show that this price solves a partial differential equation with a fractional derivative in time, which we call the time-fractional Black--Scholes equation.
item.dc:creator: Shuaiqi Zhang, Zhen-Qing Chen

item.title: Blowup for the multiplicative stochastic heat equation with superlinear drift
item.description: arXiv:2511.23403v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the stochastic heat equation with multiplicative white noise: $\partial_t u =\partial_x^2u + b(u) +\sigma(u) \dot W$, both on $[0,1]$ and $\mathbb R$. In the case of $[0,1]$ we show that the finite Osgood criterion on $b$ is a necessary and sufficient condition for finite-time blowup, under fairly general conditions on $\sigma$. In the case of $\mathbb R$ we show instantaneous explosion when we start with initial profile $u_0\equiv 1$. Our work introduces a novel approach that not only extends the work of [12] which dealt with bounded $\sigma$, but also provides an alternate route to proving such results. A key ingredient is a comparison result which shows that the solution on $\mathbb R$ stays above the corresponding solution on $[0,1]$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Mathew Joseph, Shubham Ovhal

item.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
item.description: arXiv:2512.14248v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are H\"older curves or H\"older parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hinz, Jonas M. T\"olle, Lauri Viitasaari

item.title: Pathwise solutions of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by a multiplicative Hermite noise
item.description: arXiv:2602.14617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the viscous Burgers equation on the real line perturbed by a multiplicative noise $\sigma(u)\dot{Z}_t$, where $Z$ is a Hermite process of order $q\ge1$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$; the case $q=1$ is fractional Brownian motion and $q=2$ is the Rosenblatt process. The stochastic term is a Young integral and the equation is solved path by path. A transformation of Doss-Sussmann type reduces it to a parabolic equation with random coefficients and quadratic growth in the gradient, for which we prove a maximum principle and a gradient estimate of Bernstein type on short time windows. We obtain global existence and uniqueness, the pathwise bound $|u(t,x)|\le\|u_0\|_\infty+\|\sigma\|_\infty|Z_t|$, and a Wong-Zakai type result without correction term. All moments are finite and $\mathbb{E}\exp(\lambda\sup_x|u(t,x)|^{2/q})<\infty$ for small $\lambda$. For the Rosenblatt process with $\sigma\ge\sigma_0>0$, $\mathbb{E}\,e^{\lambda u(t,x)}$ is finite for small $\lambda$ and infinite for $\lambda\sigma_0t^H\ge\theta_H$, an explicit spectral constant, while the left tail is sub-Gaussian. We show that the temporal H\"older exponent $H$ is optimal, identify the limits of the power variations of $t\mapsto u(t,x)$, and deduce consistent estimators of $H$ and of the noise intensity from one path observed at one spatial point. For $q=2$ we relate the pathwise solution to a Skorokhod formulation through the forward/Skorokhod correction formula of \v{C}oupek, Duncan and Pasik-Duncan.
item.dc:creator: Atef Lechiheb

item.title: An extension of Stein's method incorporating dependence
item.description: arXiv:2605.25206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Stein's method to include a prescribed dependence with respect to an auxiliary random variable, for conditional laws for which Stein characterizations do exist. This considerably extends the range of applications of Stein's method. The characterization we derive subsumes the case of independent random variables. Using the Malliavin calculus, we illustrate our extension on the example of a conditionally Gaussian/Beta-distributed random variable.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandar Bala\v{s}ev-Samarski, Abdol-Reza Mansouri

item.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
item.description: arXiv:2607.05693v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\to\tau$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(\tau/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.
item.dc:creator: Joon Hyung Lee

item.title: Universality transitions in the logarithmic law of random determinants beyond the fourth moment
item.description: arXiv:2609.11688v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For real random matrices $A_n=(a_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ with independent centered entries of unit variance, \citet{BaoPanZhou2015} established the classical logarithmic law under a uniform fourth-moment condition: \[ \frac{\log|\det A_n|-\frac12\log(n-1)!} {\sqrt{\frac12\log n}} \Rightarrow \mathcal N(0,1). \] We find that this Gaussian universality can be extended beyond the fourth-moment condition, with two distinct transitions in the center and fluctuation scale as the moment condition gradually weaken. The first critical condition is the uniform integrability of the family $\{|a_{ij}|^4/\sqrt{\log(e+|a_{ij}|)}\}_{n,i,j}$. The classical law remains valid under this weaker condition, with no change in center or scale. As the moment condition is weakened further, the classical center can fail. Replacing the classical center $\frac12\log(n-1)!$ by the actual mean $\mathbb E\log|\det A_n|$ preserves the standard Gaussian limit at the original scale and allows the moment condition to be relaxed to a second critical condition: uniform integrability of $\{|a_{ij}|^4/\log(e+|a_{ij}|)\}_{n,i,j}$. Under still weaker moment conditions, the classical scale $\sqrt{\frac12\log n}$ can also fail. Replacing this scale in turn by the actual standard deviation $\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\log|\det A_n|)}$ yields a standard Gaussian limit whenever the expectations of $|a_{ij}|^4/\{\log(e+|a_{ij}|)\}^{\alpha}$ are uniformly bounded over $n,i,j$, for any fixed $\alpha\ge0$. The results using the actual mean or standard deviation additionally assume uniformly bounded entry densities. We establish the sharpness of the first two critical conditions via counterexamples. We further obtain Berry--Esseen bounds for all three normalizations, with optimal rates under a uniform fourth-moment bound.
item.dc:creator: Song-Hao Liu, Qi-Man Shao, Hao Shi, Jing-Yu Xu

item.title: Phase transition for the smallest eigenvalue of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices
item.description: arXiv:2609.15731v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the sample correlation matrix $\mathbf{R}_n$ formed from a $p_n \times n$ data matrix with i.i.d. real entries $\xi$ of mean zero and unit variance, in the high-dimensional regime $p_n / n \to \phi \in (0, \infty) \setminus \{1\}$. In the tall regime $\phi > 1$, we prove almost-sure convergence of $\lambda_n (\mathbf{R}_n)$ to the lower Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur edge $\lambda_- = (1 - \sqrt{\phi})^2$ without additional moment assumptions. In the wide regime $\phi < 1$, we establish a phase transition at the third-order tail scale. If $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert \xi \rvert > t\} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$, the smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to $\lambda_-$. While if $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert \xi \rvert > t\} \to \infty$, then $\lambda_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$ converges in probability to zero. At the critical scale $t^3 \mathbb{P}\{\lvert \xi \rvert > t\} \to \kappa \in (0, \infty)$, the point process of eigenvalues in the lower gap $(0, \lambda_-)$ converges in distribution to a Poisson random measure with explicit intensity. In this critical regime, we also identify the nondegenerate limiting distribution of $\lambda_{p_n} (\mathbf{R}_n)$, which has a continuous density on $(0, \lambda_-)$ and a positive atom at $\lambda_-$.
item.dc:creator: Zeqin Lin, Guamgming Pan, Haozhu Zhao, Wang Zhou

item.title: Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
item.description: arXiv:2609.23949v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Jerschow

item.title: Localization Lengths for Two-Dimensional Random Band Matrices: Exponential Lower Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2609.24426v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{xy})$ with centered complex Gaussian entries, indexed by points $x,y$ on the two-dimensional discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z} / \sqrt{N} \mathbb{Z})^2$. The matrix entries $H_{xy}$ vanish whenever the distance between $x$ and $y$ exceeds a constant multiple of the bandwidth parameter $W$. We prove that, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if $W\geq(\log N)^{1+\varepsilon}$, then all bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with high probability. Equivalently, this yields a lower bound of order $\exp(W^{1-\varepsilon})$ on the localization length of two-dimensional random band matrices for arbitrarily small constant $\varepsilon>0$, improving the superpolynomial lower bound $W^C$ for every fixed constant $C>0$ established in arXiv:2503.07606. A key ingredient of our proof is a new strategy that closes the resolvent flow analysis using only loop observables of order at most two, without relying on the higher-order loop hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Xujie Lai, Fan Yang

item.title: Quantitative QSD convergence in 1-Wasserstein distance via the F\"ollmer drift
item.description: arXiv:2609.29042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a novel pathwise approach to study the convergence of the law of killed diffusion processes conditioned on non-absorption, towards a quasi-stationary distribution (QSD) as time goes to infinity. We start from the general observation that the dynamics of an absorbed Markov process conditioned upon survival up to time $T>0$ is the minimizer of the pathwise relative entropy with respect to its unconditioned dynamics, under a simple distributional constraint at that time; in other words, a F\"ollmer process. We then show how this result applies to a Brownian diffusion process softly-killed at a state-dependent regular rate, and characterize the minimizer and its drift change. In the case when the diffusion process is moreover reversible, we leverage these ideas and recent results on the propagation of weak log-concavity of HJB semigroups to prove that, under strict asymptotic convexity of the potential, the conditioned dynamics satisfies a contractivity property in $1$-Wasserstein distance, uniformly in $T>0$. We then establish the existence of a QSD with a large domain of attraction and deduce the exponentially fast convergence to it of the conditioned semigroup in the $1$-Wasserstein distance as $T$ goes to infinity. Finally, we deduce the exponentially fast convergence, also in $1$-Wasserstein distance, of the law of the corresponding Q-process towards its equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Joaqu\'in Fontbona, Pablo L\'opez-Rivera

item.title: Conditional Fluctuations of Mean-Field Systems with Stable Common Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.01391v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study conditional fluctuations of smooth mean-field systems on a torus with symmetric stable common jumps of index $0<\alpha<1$. A positive-strip estimate makes empirical Poisson acceptance errors negligible at the sampling scale. Given the full Poisson master, the conditional laws converge in probability to a centered Gaussian kernel in a negative Sobolev path space. In dimension one, quantile coupling preserves this limit for microscopic marks with relative tail remainder $O(x^{-\rho})$, where $\rho>\tfrac{\alpha}{2}$. A second-order tail expansion identifies the response when this condition fails: it shifts the conditional Gaussian mean at criticality and, when nonzero, dominates sampling below criticality. We also identify the transition from a stable to a Brownian rank error. In a translation model, rank and clock couplings give the same microscopic laws but different path fluctuations. Rank coupling gives a functional Gaussian limit. Clock coupling admits no diverging additive path normalization at the limiting center.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Autran

item.title: Second-order Wasserstein response for L\'evy laws
item.description: arXiv:2610.01411v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Moving an atom and splitting it symmetrically can give the same weak change in a L\'evy characteristic, yet produce Wasserstein errors of different orders. We explain this through first- and second-order expansions of the distribution function for infinitely divisible laws with a Gaussian factor. The expansions are uniform over Lipschitz tests and include distributional directions from moving atoms. When the first response is nonzero, analyticity gives the signed second coefficient of the Wasserstein--1 distance. When it vanishes, a finite second displacement moment gives a quadratic response, with a positive coefficient whenever the dispersion is nonzero. For local balanced remeshing, we prove matching bounds in terms of grid-alignment variance and construct a linear program with a controlled optimization gap. We also determine the sharp transition as Gaussian smoothing vanishes. The appendices give proofs, metric speed and length, and multivariate and state-dependent extensions.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Autran

item.title: The Right Wing of the SABR Smile with an Absorbing Boundary: Resolution of Conjectures of Henry-Labord\`ere
item.description:
arXiv:2610.04209v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the fixed-maturity right tail of the SABR model with $ eta\in(0,1)$ absorbed at zero, for every correlation $ho$: the probability $P(k)$ that the forward ends above $f_0e^k$ satisfies $-k^{-2}\ln P(k)	o(1- eta)^2/(2
u^2T(1-(ho\wedge0)^2))$. The implied volatility therefore tends to $
u\sqrt{1-(ho\wedge0)^2}/(1- eta)$. Henry-Labord\`ere's conjectured limit $
u/(1- eta)$, which Hagan's leading-order formula also gives, holds for $ho\ge0$ and fails for $ho<0$, where survival keeps the noise orthogonal to volatility above a moving square-root barrier. The Gaussian estimate behind his second conjecture does not hold for $ho<0$; the rate is instead given by the intrinsic distance within the survival domain.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Cao, Shaosai Huang

item.title: Staircase phase transitions for the extreme eigenvalues of heavy-tailed sample correlation matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.06731v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish phase transitions in the first-order asymptotics of the largest and smallest nonzero eigenvalues of high-dimensional sample correlation matrices formed from data with i.i.d. centered real entries of finite variance, allowing an infinite fourth moment. Because of self-normalization, spectral outliers are driven by collisions of large entries in distinct rows of a common column rather than by individual large entries. The resulting phase transitions depend jointly on the aspect ratio and the entry tail, producing staircase boundaries in the phase diagram. We prove convergence to the corresponding Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur edges in subcritical regimes and to deterministic outlier levels in supercritical regimes. In critical regimes, Poisson limits for the point processes of spectral outliers and nondegenerate limiting laws for the extreme eigenvalues are established.
item.dc:creator: Yanpeng Li, Zeqin Lin, Yiming Liu, Jiahui Xie, Haozhu Zhao

item.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincar\'e Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.07728v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincar\'e constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincar\'e constant $C_P(\mu)\le25$, where $\mu$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincar\'e inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.
item.dc:creator: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Shiva Kasiviswanathan

item.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20299v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Aubrun, Emmanouil Stavrakakis

item.title: Perron--Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for inhomogeneous random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23003v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and continuous compact type kernels satisfying a positivity condition. Let $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u d\mu=1$, and put $\alpha=\int u^2 d\mu$ and $\beta=\int u^3 d\mu$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $\rho$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $\rho(1)=1$ and $\log\rho(t)=\frac{\alpha^2}{2\beta}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L<\infty$, $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)=w_r\beta^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}\rho(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At criticality, the leading constant depends on the kernel only through $\beta$, under the stated normalization of $u$. At $t_n=1+\lambda n^{-1/3}$, exact component identities combine with these asymptotics to give fixed size factorial densities and local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollob\'as-Janson-Riordan models. With sizes rescaled by $\beta^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $\alpha\beta^{-2/3}\lambda$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)\mu(dx)$. For every bounded uniformly positive countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Hu, Wen Sun

item.title: Deterministic Principal Ideals of Dependent Random Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.03495v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the algebraic principal ideals of alternating quadratic random operators under dimension-free two-sided curvature bounds. For the centered evaluation of a Hilbert two-form, an explicit covariance compensator determines the principal ideal after every fixed compact perturbation. For fixed spectral choices, the compensator is a compact linear function of the full covariance with explicit finite-dimensional approximation bounds; its class modulo the independent Gaussian ideal is intrinsic. For fixed spatial weights of rank at least two and a trace-class kernel, all attainable principal ideals form an exact order interval. Every intermediate ideal is realized by a Gaussian covariance arbitrarily close to the identity while each row retains its standard Gaussian law. For these spatial weights, trace class is also the exact kernel domain for raw evaluation under every law in the curvature class. The proof uses a conditional-residual criterion for linear operators, polarization, and finite-rank approximation. Applications include Wiener area and dependent matrices with doubly monotone variance weights. A logarithmic example separates principal ideals with identical membership in every Schatten class.
item.dc:creator: Guangqian Zhao

item.title: The critical Cauchy boundary for Gibbs partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study critical Gibbs partitions whose component law is in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive stable law of index one. In the dense phase, we prove a local limit theorem for the number of components and functional limits for their sizes. We also describe convergent and divergent condensation regimes, and a phase transition at a boundary in which the dense and condensation contributions compete.
item.dc:creator: Fabien Baeriswyl, Benedikt Stufler

item.title: Validity of the Behrens--Fisher solution
item.description: arXiv:2611.06987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Behrens--Fisher fiducial interval for the difference of two normal means is known from the numerical work of Robinson (1976) to be conservative, but a proof has been lacking. The results here prove that the fiducial interval for any linear combination of $k$ normal means has coverage probability at least its nominal level for all values of the unknown variances. Taraldsen (2026) explains this in more detail using the original data of Behrens (1926). The proof presented in the following rests on a novel plug-in inequality: if a threshold function controls a scaled sum of pivots pointwise in the scale vector, then it also controls the sum with the observed scales plugged in, provided the location errors satisfy a concentration condition formulated through a weighted geometric mean. Independent normal errors satisfy the condition.
item.dc:creator: Gunnar Taraldsen

item.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the martingale property of stochastic exponentials driven by multi-dimensional diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give necessary and sufficient coefficient conditions for stochastic exponentials driven by multidimensional diffusions to be true martingales. The classical reduction to non-exit of the diffusion with Girsanov-shifted drift separates the analysis into smooth boundary points, infinity, and nonsmooth boundary pieces. On smooth domains, under regularity and non-explosion hypotheses, martingality is equivalent to nonpositivity of the shifted Fichera drift, provided an explicit local condition holds where that drift vanishes and the stochastic integrand is unbounded. At infinity, Feller's test gives exact criteria when a scalar function of the diffusion reduces to a one-dimensional diffusion up to a time change with rate comparable to a positive function of the scalar coordinate. General radial and projection tests supply sufficient conditions. Applications give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for inverse-CIR and $4/2$ models with correlated factors and singular stochastic integrands, including critical equality cases. The coupled non-affine examples go beyond direct scalar Feller tests and affine Riccati criteria, and exhibit boundary exits not decided by tests at infinity. Further exact criteria cover logarithmic boundary singularities, weighted distances, and an absorbed factor. The martingale conditions also yield uniqueness criteria for associated valuation equations.
item.dc:creator: Erhan Bayraktar, Hao Xing

item.title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $\beta=2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $\beta=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by D\"urr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).
item.dc:creator: Hirofumi Osada, Kohei Suzuki

item.title: Local and global existence for the stochastic Prandtl equation driven by multiplicative noises in two and three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2408.04546v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the local and global existence for the stochastic Prandtl equation in two and three dimensions, which governs the velocity field inside the boundary layer that appears in the inviscid limit of the stochastic Navier-Stokes equation with non-slip boundary condition. New problem arises when establishing the well-posedness in the stochastic regime: one can never derive a pathwise control of the energy functional which is used to describe the analytic radius of the solution in the deterministic setting. To this end, we establish higher-order estimates in the conormal Sobolev spaces in order to get rid of the dependence of the analytic radius on the unknown. Three approximate schemes are constructed for solving the stochastic Prandtl equation, and a local well-posedness is obtained in a tangentially analytic and normally Sobolev-type space. Furthermore, we study the stochastic Prandtl equation driven by a tangential random diffusion, and find that the noise regularizes the equation in the sense that in both two and three dimensions, there exists a global Gevrey-2 solution with high probability and the radius growing linearly in time.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Guang Wang, Meng Zhao

item.title: Polynomial mixing for the white-forced Navier-Stokes system in the whole space
item.description: arXiv:2410.15727v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the mixing properties of the white-forced Navier-Stokes system in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^2$. Assuming that the noise is sufficiently non-degenerate, we prove the uniqueness of stationary measure and polynomial mixing in the dual-Lipschitz metric. The proof combines the coupling method with a Foia\c{s}-Prodi type estimate, weighted growth estimates for trajectories, and an estimate for the Leray projector involving Muckenhoupt $A_2$-class weights.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Nersesyan, Meng Zhao

item.title: Continuous-time mean field games: a primal-dual characterization
item.description: arXiv:2503.01042v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper establishes a primal-dual formulation for continuous-time mean field games (MFGs) and provides a complete analytical characterization of the set of all mean field equilibria (MFEs). We reformulate the representative player's control problem as a linear program over occupation measures and derive its dual formulation over smooth subsolutions of the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation. This primal-dual formulation yields a verification theorem for MFEs under measurable coefficients and provides necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing all MFEs under a strong duality condition. We establish this strong duality for nondegenerate diffusions with H\"older continuous coefficients through a new global $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity result for fully nonlinear parabolic HJB equations. A key insight is that the dual variable need only coincide with the HJB solution on the support of the mean field flow. Compared with existing approaches, our characterization requires neither convexity of the Hamiltonian nor uniqueness of its optimizer, accommodates relaxed equilibria, and remains applicable when the HJB equation lacks classical solutions.
item.dc:creator: Xin Guo, Anran Hu, Jiacheng Zhang, Yufei Zhang

item.title: M-estimation for Gaussian processes with time-inhomogeneous drifts from high-frequency data
item.description: arXiv:2508.01164v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study drift and covariance estimation for a stationary Gaussian process with an integrated deterministic drift, observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of an increment least-squares estimator under conditions on drift accumulation and the full covariance of the weighted increments. For directly Riemann integrable drifts, this estimator need not be consistent, as an explicit example shows. Covariance parameters can nevertheless be estimated consistently when the drift decays sufficiently fast. For smooth short-range kernels, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the centered sample variance and the normalized increment second moment, with rate $\sqrt{T_n}$. These statistics require no drift estimate and identify both parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The results clarify how drift accumulation and increment dependence affect the two estimation problems.
item.dc:creator: Yasutaka Shimizu

item.title: Noise estimation of SDE from a single data trajectory
item.description: arXiv:2509.25484v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose a pathwise data-driven framework for model discovery of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) from a single trajectory, without requiring the ergodicity or stationary assumption on the underlying continuous process. By combining (stochastic) Taylor expansions with Girsanov transformations, and using the drift function's initial value as input, we construct drift estimators while simultaneously recovering the model noise. This drift is unique up to the fixed underlying Brownian sample path, in line with pathwise unique Rough-Smooth decomposition. This allows us to recover the underlying $\mathbb P$ Brownian motion increments for the observer path $\omega$. Building on these estimators, we introduce the first stochastic Sparse Identification of Stochastic Differential Equation (SSISDE) algorithm, capable of identifying the governing SDE dynamics from a single observed trajectory without requiring ergodicity or stationarity. To validate the proposed approach, we conduct numerical experiments with both linear and quadratic drift-diffusion functions. Among these, the Black-Scholes SDE is included as a representative case of a system that does not satisfy ergodicity or stationarity.
item.dc:creator: Munawar Ali, Purba Das, Qi Feng, Liyao Gao, Guang Lin

item.title: A formula for the edge density $\sqrt{n}$-correction for two-dimensional Coulomb systems
item.description: arXiv:2510.16945v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In connection with recent work on smallest gaps, C. Charlier proves that the 1-point function of a suitable planar Coulomb system $\{z_j\}_1^n$, in the determinantal case with respect to an external potential $Q(z)$, admits the expansion, as $n\to\infty$, $$R_n\bigg(z_0+\frac t {\sqrt{2n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}}\nu(z_0)\bigg)=n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)\frac {\operatorname{erfc} t}2+\sqrt{n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}\,C(z_0;t)+\mathcal{O}(\log^6 n).$$ Here $t$ is a real parameter, $z_0$ is a regular boundary point of the (connected) Coulomb droplet and $\nu(z_0)$ is the outwards unit normal; the coefficient $C(z_0;t)$ has an apriori structure depending on a number of parameters. In this note we identify the parameters and obtain a formula for $C(z_0;t)$ in potential theoretic and geometric terms. Our formula holds for a large class of potentials such that the droplet is connected with smooth boundary. Our derivation uses the well known expectation of fluctuations formula.
item.dc:creator: Yacin Ameur

item.title: Large-Time Analysis of the Langevin Dynamics for Energies Fulfilling Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2510.24925v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we take a step towards understanding overdamped Langevin dynamics for the minimization of a general class of objective functions $\mathcal{L}$. We establish well-posedness and regularity of the law $\rho_t$ of the process through novel a priori estimates, and, very importantly, we characterize the large-time behavior of $\rho_t$ under truly minimal assumptions on $\mathcal{L}$. In the case of integrable Gibbs density, the law converges to the normalized Gibbs measure. In the non-integrable case, we prove that the law diffuses. The rate of convergence, in terms of relative Dirichlet energy with respect to the Gibbs measure, is $\mathcal O(1/(\sigma t))$, where $\sigma$ is the diffusion parameter. Under a Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on $\mathcal{L}$, we also derive sharp exponential contractivity results toward the set of global minimizers. Combining these results we provide the first systematic convergence analysis of Langevin dynamics under PL conditions in non-integrable Gibbs settings: a first phase of exponential in time contraction toward the set of minimizers and then a large-time exploration over it with rate $\mathcal O(1/(\sigma t))$ in terms of the relative Dirichlet energy.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Fornasier, Lukang Sun, Rachel Ward

item.title: Control policies for a two-stage queueing system with parallel and single server options
item.description: arXiv:2601.13576v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a two-stage queueing system attended by two flexible servers. Once a server begins to interact with a job, it remains attached to its job throughout both stages of service. After completing the first-stage service, the server chooses between two second-stage options. Option 1 sends the server-job pair to a parallel-service station where both servers may operate simultaneously; therefore, the server immediately begins the second-stage service on its job. Option 2 routes the pair to a single-service station that admits at most one server-job pair into service at a time. While we consider the complete range of parameters, the usual reason for choosing Option 2 is that jobs may receive higher-quality (faster and/or lower expected cost) service. If the single-service station is occupied, the pair must wait together until the station becomes available. The decision-making scenario is modeled via a Markov decision process formulation of a clearing system with holding costs at each station. Focusing on cases with a large initial queue, we fully characterize the structural properties of an optimal control policy based on the relationship between the service rates at the downstream stations. A numerical study highlights the significance of understanding the structure of the optimal policy by comparing its performance against several natural heuristic policies.
item.dc:creator: Shuwen Lu, Mark E. Lewis, Jamol Pender

item.title: Conditional Independence under Infinite Measures and Poisson Point Processes
item.description: arXiv:2604.01399v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study conditional independence under infinite measures on punctured product spaces, a notion recently introduced for graphical modeling in multivariate extremes and L\'evy processes. In contrast to classical probabilistic conditional independence, this concept is formulated through normalized restrictions of an infinite measure, a formulation that reflects the non-product structure of the punctured space. We show that this non-standard notion admits a natural probabilistic characterization: it is equivalent to classical conditional independence between coordinate projections of a Poisson point process defined on the punctured space with the given infinite measure as its mean measure. In addition, we provide a functional characterization of the conditional independence concept at the level of the enumerated points of the Poisson point process. We further extend the characterization to punctured products of Borel spaces with distinguished points and a product localization.
item.dc:creator: Shuyang Bai, Vishal Routh

item.title: Self-organized regime switching in null-recurrent dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.25368v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Based on discrete observations $X_0,X_{\Delta},\dots, X_{n\Delta}$ for $\Delta=n^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma\in [0,1)$ of the null-recurrent dynamic $dX_t = \sigma(X_t)dW_t$ with a Brownian motion $W$ and $\sigma(x)=\alpha\mathbb{1}\{x<\rho\} + \beta\mathbb{1}\{x\geq \rho\}$, we derive rate of convergence and limiting distribution of the profile MLE for $\rho$. This includes low-frequency asymptotics ($\gamma=0$) for which the observations form a null-recurrent Markov chain. The derived non-standard limit is the argsup over a doubly stochastic drifted Poisson process explicitly involving the local time of oscillating Brownian motion. Its dependence on $\rho$ as well as the unknown volatility levels $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is shown to be continuous w.r.t. the topology of weak convergence, enabling statistical inference. Whereas this limit is independent of the sampling frequency, the profile MLE's rate of convergence equals $n^{-(1+\gamma)/2}$ and is proven to be minimax optimal. The surprising idea of the proof of the limit theorem is to relate the long-term behavior of the null-recurrent Markov chain to the infill asymptotics on a fixed time interval. Indeed, in the very special case that $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is started in the true parameter $X_0=\rho_0$, the process $(X_t-\rho_0)_{t\geq 0}$ is shown to possess a desirable distributional self-similarity. On basis of the strong Markov property, the artificial constellation of starting in $\rho_0$ is finally overcome by a coupling argument.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Brutsche, Sebastian Hahn, Angelika Rohde

item.title: Understanding Simulated Annealing: from Weak Poincar\'e Inequalities to a Discrete Optimal Transport Framework
item.description: arXiv:2605.05877v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Simulated annealing follows a path of distributions from an easy initial law to a target. Standard analyses require rapid mixing at every fixed temperature, which can fail for multimodal targets even when annealing succeeds. Motivated by the continuous optimal-transport analysis of annealed Langevin dynamics by Guo, Tao, and Chen (ICLR 2025), we develop a discrete optimal-transport framework for finite-state annealing. The discrete action of the path integrates the minimum electrical energy needed to route the demand $-\partial_s\pi_s$ through the chain's transition capacities. Like a path-dependent inverse conductance, it penalizes a bottleneck only when the path must move mass across it. We also introduce weak action, which leaves an $\varepsilon$ amount of this motion unrouted. Up to initialization error, action $\mathcal A$ gives reverse-KL error at most $\mathcal A/(4T)$ after $T$ expected updates, while weak action gives TV error at most $\varepsilon+\sqrt{\mathcal A^{w}_\varepsilon/(8T)}$. Paralleling canonical paths and Poincar\'e inequalities, we develop flow and spectral bounds, showing that pathwise (weak) Poincar\'e inequalities imply (weak) action bounds. We also show that a weak Poincar\'e inequality yields a genuine one after removing a small amount of mass. As a pathwise analogue of chain decomposition, we obtain a componentwise algorithm for mixtures with phase weights supplied at initialization. Applications include mean-field Ising and Potts models and bipartite spin systems. For every fixed $\delta>0$, we give a polynomial-time single-site annealing sampler for uniform independent sets in $(d,D)$-biregular bipartite graphs with $D/d\geq1+\delta$ and large $D$. To our knowledge, this is the first polynomial-time sampler requiring only a fixed multiplicative degree imbalance, strictly extending the $D\geq7d\log d$ regime of Cannon and Perkins (SODA 2020).
item.dc:creator: Yuchen He, Tianhui Jiang, Zhehan Lei, Sihan Wang, Chihao Zhang

item.title: Spanning triangulations in random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.20361v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 1991 Bollob\'{a}s and Frieze found the threshold for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a triangle in the binomial random graph, up to a logarithmic factor. In this paper, we find the threshold probability for the emergence of a spanning triangulation of a $k$-gon for any $3\leq k\leq n$, up to a constant factor.
item.dc:creator: S. Vakhrushev, M. Zhukovskii

item.title: An optimal local theory for reaction-diffusion equations driven by non-trace-class noise
item.description: arXiv:2606.07417v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study local well-posedness for a class of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations driven by multiplicative, possibly colored, noise. The interaction between rough stochastic forcing and polynomial nonlinearities naturally leads to solutions with low spatial regularity, making the treatment of the nonlinear terms delicate. Our main contribution is a general local existence and uniqueness theory for SPDEs with rough noise and highly irregular initial data. The framework also yields new results in standard noise regimes, including trace-class noise and space-time white noise. We identify the critical initial-data spaces for a wide range of nonlinearities, and we establish instantaneous parabolic regularization, general blow-up criteria, and sufficient conditions for positivity preservation. We apply the abstract theory to several prototypical models, including the stochastic Allen-Cahn, Burgers, Fisher-KPP, and coupled Gray-Scott equations. Finally, in the one-dimensional space-time white-noise setting, we combine our local theory with existing global a priori results in a highly singular regime.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Agresti, Fabian Germ, Mark Veraar

item.title: Lyapunov-Based Sample Complexity Analysis for Weakly-Coupled MDPs
item.description: arXiv:2606.14095v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the sample complexity of learning in average-reward weakly-coupled Markov decision processes (WCMDPs) and Restless Bandits (RBs) under a generative model. Naive reduction to a tabular MDP leads to high complexity bounds as the state-action space is exponentially large in the number of arms $N$. By exploiting the weakly coupled structure, we show that near-optimal policies can be learned with sample and computational complexities that are polynomial in $N$. Specifically, we analyze the plug-in approach, which applies an efficient planning algorithm to an empirical model estimated from data. For fully heterogeneous WCMDPs, we establish the first finite-sample PAC guarantee with polynomial complexity and an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap. For homogeneous RBs, we further prove that a smaller optimality gap is achievable under mild structural assumptions. A primary technical contribution is a novel Lyapunov-based analysis framework. Unlike classical approaches that rely on the difficult-to-control bias function, our framework uses an explicitly constructed Lyapunov function along with a drift transfer technique between the true and empirical models. A key step of independent interest in our framework is a fine-grained perturbation analysis for the underlying linear programming (LP) relaxation, which provides a general tool for analyzing LP-based policies and weakly-coupled systems.
item.dc:creator: Tianhao Wu, Matthew Zurek, Weina Wang, Qiaomin Xie

item.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
item.description: arXiv:2607.17469v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $\nu$ with $\nu[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth. This tree max-flow/min-cut identity makes worst-case probabilities exact and optimizable. Three applications follow. In scheduling, $n$ tasks on one machine are each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set; every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-\Theta(n)]$, and a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment satisfying a majority of each clause, we find the sharp source threshold $s_*$: below it, on some instances one admissible source forces nontermination for every clause selection; at it, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial distance, against linear under independence, with matching instances at distances up to a constant fraction of the number of variables; a fixed margin above it restores linear dependence. For noisy predecessor search with prefix-bounded comparison errors, verified backtracking attains any prescribed error probability at or above a source threshold whose sharpness we leave open, with the same cubic-to-linear query bounds. Restarting on the shared tape restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.
item.dc:creator: Yunbei Xu

item.title: The Zaporozhets-Tarasov Conjecture on Mean Distances
item.description: arXiv:2608.06470v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a convex body $K \subset \mathbb R^d$ let $\Delta(K)$ be the expected distance between two independent uniform points of $K$, and let $\theta(K)$ be the corresponding expectation for normalized surface measure on $\partial K$. The Zaporozhets-Tarasov conjecture asserts $\Delta(K) \le \theta(K)$. We prove this conjecture in case $d=2$. In addition, we give a six-vertex convex polytope in $\mathbb R^3$ for which the reverse strict inequality holds, and obtain counterexamples in every dimension $d \ge 3$ by taking products with segments.
item.dc:creator: Eric Shen

item.title: Limits of Stochastic Semigroups and Block-Triangular Majorisation
item.description: arXiv:2609.04057v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate limits of semigroups of stochastic matrices defined by their invariant distribution. Given probability vectors $q(\beta)$ depending on a parameter $\beta$, we introduce a notion of convergence as $\beta\to\infty$ for the corresponding semigroups of $q(\beta)$-preserving stochastic matrices and investigate the structure of the resulting limit. In general, the limiting semigroup differs from the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, showing that these two operations do not commute. We develop a general framework for such limiting semigroups and study in detail the case in which the invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors at inverse temperature $\beta$. In that case, the limiting semigroup consists of block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices subject to additional substochasticity constraints. We characterise and enumerate their extremal elements and determine the preorder on probability vectors induced by the action of the semigroup. The resulting notion of Block-Triangular majorisation interpolates between ordinary majorisation and upper triangular (also known as unordered) majorisation. We show that it is completely characterised by a finite family of monotones and analyse the corresponding behaviour of R{\'e}nyi $\alpha$-entropies as $\beta\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Jakub Czartowski, Giovanni Gramegna, Marilena Ligab\`o

item.title: A New Approach to Universal Measurability
item.description: arXiv:2609.14414v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: V. Fedorchuk, A. Chigogidze and T. Banakh in 2003 and V. Bogachev in 2024 posed the following questions: (i) is it true that $P_\tau(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_\sigma(X)$; (ii) is it true that $P_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_R(\beta X)$ if and only if $X$ is pseudocompact, where $P_\sigma$, $P_\tau$ and $P_R$ are the functors of probability measures on the space $X$ that are, respectively, $\sigma$-additive on the Baire $\sigma$-algebra, $\tau$-additive, and Radon? The answers to these questions are negative. In this paper the questions are put into a general framework: for spaces of measures $Q_p(X)\subset Q_q(X)$ of various types we study when $Q_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $Q_q(X)$. It is proved that for spaces of alternating measures $M_p(X)\subset M_q(X)$ the $C$-embeddedness, the $C^*$-embeddedness and the $G_\delta$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and a criterion in terms of sequences of continuous functions is given. The question of $C$-embedding of measure spaces is an extension of the question of coincidence of measure spaces, which is a development of the classical concepts of universally measurable and universal measure zero sets. Note (corrected version): incorrect statements of the previous versions are marked or removed; see the last section of the paper.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: E. A. Reznichenko and Yu V. Sadovnichiy. A new approach to universal measurement. Bulletin of the Institute of Mathematics of the National Academy of Sciences of the Kyrgyz Republic, (2):2, 2025
item.dc:creator: Reznichenko E. A., Sadovnichiy Yu. V

item.title: A Log-Star Comparison Between Expectation Threshold and Fractional Expectation Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2609.30680v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We proved a log-star comparison between the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ and the fractional expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ for any nontrivial increasing family $\mathcal F$ on a finite ground set $V$ of size $|V|=N$. Specifically, we show that $$q_f(\mathcal F)\le64\log_2^*(N+2)\,q(\mathcal F),$$ where $\log_2^* x$ is the iterated logarithm of base-2. Using similiar methods, one can extend this result to the following stronger form: there exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that \[ q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(l(\mathcal F)),\quad q_f(\mathcal F)\le Cq(\mathcal F)\log_2^*(\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)), \] where $l(\mathcal F):=\max\{2,\max_{S\in\min\mathcal F}|S|\}$ and $\operatorname{VC}(\min\mathcal F)$ denotes the VC-dimension of $\min\mathcal F$. On October 7, 2026, OpenAI released a result proving the equivalence of fractional and integral thresholds, which supersedes the findings in this note. The authors are keeping this note for historical reference.

item.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
item.description: arXiv:2610.16955v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.

item.title: A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets
item.description: arXiv:2610.24169v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding Hilbert-space-valued Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for both strong and mild solutions. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. We also establish asymptotic completeness through finite-dimensional noise truncations. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.

item.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.30166v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.

item.title: Holomorphic Cauchy Networks for Efficient Stationary Tail Computation in High-Dimensional Reflected Brownian Motions
item.description: arXiv:2610.36558v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stationary tail computation for high-dimensional reflected Brownian motions (RBMs) remains computationally challenging. Building on NN4MGF's shared-coordinate basic-adjoint-relationship (BAR) framework, we develop Holomorphic Cauchy Networks (HCNs). Native complex-valued rational Cauchy subnetworks enforce holomorphicity on pole-free domains, removing sampled Cauchy-Riemann penalties and their input-derivative graphs. Exact origin anchoring and boundary-coordinate exclusion enforce structural identities, while anchored interactions represent dependent transforms. Under holomorphic-log assumptions, we establish simultaneous value and first-derivative approximation for the constrained architectures and a mixed-derivative lower bound for coordinate-only representations under nonzero cross-covariance. Closed-form real-axis derivatives and sequential backpropagation further control memory. On the same NVIDIA H100 NVL, the tested 30D HCN configuration uses approximately tenfold less peak allocated memory and has 9.7-fold lower mean update time than NN4MGF; extrapolation to the respective scheduled update counts gives a projected full-schedule update-time ratio of 58.2. With 64 million sampled base inputs per high-dimensional run, HCN reaches 50 dimensions on a laptop GPU with 6.367% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8. Degree-matched comparisons yield lower reported mean relative errors over the primary evaluation ranges, including 1.422% versus 6.684% on the 2D Harrison non-product benchmark. On a 10D correlated RBM benchmark, HCN achieves 3.829% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8 against a simulation reference, compared with 19.386% for an independent-marginal baseline.

item.title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.37413v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove early-stopped, target-to-output KL guarantees for Brownian interpolant Euler sampling from the true source under arbitrary Borel couplings, even with nonintegrable endpoints. At fixed stopping time and noise level, a fourth displacement moment yields an $O(N^{-1})$ discretization term. A second moment suffices for fixed-law convergence with grid refinement and vanishing drift error. For one fixed coupling with no displacement moment above two, the original and comparison paths have KL of orders one and $1/\log N$ relative to the exact-drift Euler path. On the same geometric grid, terminal KL is at most $C/N^2$. The path decomposition identifies the information about the source discarded by Markov projection. When the original bridge is Markov, current-state Euler sampling has an $O((M_2+d)/N)$ discretization term. We prove expected stopped-output KL consistency for a learner trained on iid endpoint pairs with fresh true-source initialization. In a spatial image control, iterative sampling has worse fair energy scores than direct prediction with resampled residuals. Uniform terminal rates for general second-moment couplings remain open.

item.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.01586v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions as well as H\"{o}lder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.

item.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. Its remaining life expectancy has no known closed form, and numerical evaluation alone does not reveal how the immaturity hazard enters it. We show that the remaining-lifetime distribution at age $x$ is Gompertz--Makeham with a Poisson-distributed Makeham term. Successive Makeham terms differ by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines, and the Poisson mean is the cumulative immaturity hazard remaining after age $x$. In a latent-clock construction, individuals carry a Poisson number of constant-rate clocks, and selection removes those carrying more clocks first. Integrating the mixture yields an exact series for remaining life expectancy with a closed-form truncation bound. The life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality is close to the probability of carrying a clock times life expectancy with that hazard removed, with a closed-form error bound. In annual fits to Swedish female mortality, this loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, a decline equal to 15\% of the gain in life expectancy at birth, and the approximation was always within 0.06 years.
